title: Applied Machine Learning
tagline: The big three carry most of the weight; the rest are tools you reach for when a problem asks for them.

clusters.label: Learning paradigms
clusters.summary: How a model is told what 'better' means.

clusters.label: Modelling craft
clusters.summary: The unglamorous work that decides whether a model is usable.

clusters.label: Evaluation & judgement
clusters.summary: Knowing whether the thing actually works.

nodes.label: Supervised learning
nodes.summary: Learn a mapping from inputs to labelled outputs, then check that it holds on data the model never saw.
keyPoints: Almost every production ML system in industry is supervised.
The label definition is a product decision, not a data-cleaning step.
Generalisation is the whole game: train/validation/test discipline comes before model choice.

nodes.label: Unsupervised learning
nodes.summary: Find structure — clusters, embeddings, anomalies — when no label exists.
keyPoints: Useful for segmentation, deduplication, and retrieval, rarely for a headline metric.
Evaluation is genuinely hard: there is no ground truth to score against.
Embeddings are the version of this that most enterprise systems actually ship.

nodes.label: Self-supervised pretraining
nodes.summary: Manufacture labels from the data itself, so a model can learn from a corpus nobody annotated.
keyPoints: The reason foundation models exist: the internet becomes a training signal.
Downstream work becomes fine-tuning or prompting rather than training from scratch.
Shifts cost from labelling to compute and data curation.

nodes.label: Deep learning
nodes.summary: Stacked differentiable layers that learn their own features instead of being handed them.
keyPoints: Wins where raw signal is high-dimensional: text, image, audio, sequences.
Backpropagation plus gradient descent is the entire training loop, everything else is architecture.
On small tabular datasets, gradient-boosted trees usually still beat it.

nodes.label: Transformers & attention
nodes.summary: Attention lets every token look at every other token, which made scale pay off.
keyPoints: Self-attention is quadratic in sequence length — context length is a cost decision.
The same block powers text, vision, and multimodal models.
Understanding attention is what makes RAG, context windows, and prompt design intelligible.

nodes.label: Optimisation & training loops
nodes.summary: Loss functions, learning rates, and regularisation — the dials that decide whether training converges.
keyPoints: The loss function encodes what you actually want; most 'model bugs' are loss bugs.
Learning rate schedule matters more than optimiser choice.
Overfitting is diagnosed from the gap between training and validation curves, not from a single number.

nodes.label: Reinforcement learning
nodes.summary: An agent learns a policy by acting, observing rewards, and updating — no labelled answer key.
keyPoints: Framed as states, actions, rewards, and a policy that maximises long-run return.
The exploration/exploitation trade-off has no universally right setting.
Reward design is the hardest part: agents optimise what you measure, not what you meant.

resources.label: BFS or DFS?
resources.note: State-space search, the substrate under planning

nodes.label: RL from human feedback
nodes.summary: Use human preference data to shape a model's behaviour when the objective can't be written down.
keyPoints: Preferences replace a hand-written reward function.
This is how instruction-following and refusal behaviour get trained into language models.
Preference data quality caps the result — noisy raters produce a noisy policy.

nodes.label: Bandits & online learning
nodes.summary: The one-step case of RL: choose an arm, observe the payoff, adapt.
keyPoints: The practical entry point to RL in product work — ranking, pricing, layout tests.
Cheaper and safer to deploy than full sequential RL.
Needs a live feedback loop, which is an engineering problem more than a modelling one.

nodes.label: Features & data quality
nodes.summary: Most of the accuracy in a real system comes from the inputs, not the architecture.
keyPoints: Feature availability at inference time is a hard constraint — check it before modelling.
Training/serving skew is the most common silent failure.
A clear grain and a clear time boundary prevent most leakage.

nodes.label: Leakage & drift
nodes.summary: Two ways a model looks better offline than it will ever behave in production.
keyPoints: Leakage: information from the future or from the label sneaks into a feature.
Drift: the world moves and yesterday's mapping stops holding.
Both are detected by monitoring, not by a smarter training run.

nodes.label: Model selection & tuning
nodes.summary: Search over models and hyperparameters, honestly, without touching the test set.
keyPoints: Cross-validation buys reliability on small data and costs compute on large data.
Start with a boring baseline; it decides whether anything else is worth it.
Tuning gains are usually smaller than feature or label gains.

nodes.label: Evaluation design
nodes.summary: Choosing metrics and test sets that predict real behaviour rather than flatter the model.
keyPoints: Pick the metric from the cost of each error type, not from convention.
Hold out by time or by entity when rows are not independent.
For generative systems, build a graded question set before you build the system.

nodes.label: From metric to decision
nodes.summary: A model creates value when it changes a decision, not when it scores well.
keyPoints: Name the decision, its frequency, and the cost of being wrong before modelling.
A slightly worse model that is faster or more explainable often wins.
Offline lift and online lift diverge; plan the experiment that connects them.

nodes.label: Serving & feedback loops
nodes.summary: Inference paths, latency budgets, and the loop that returns outcomes to the training set.
keyPoints: Batch, streaming, and request/response serving have different failure modes.
Log the inputs and the prediction, or you can never diagnose a regression.
A model that changes user behaviour contaminates its own future training data.
